senses.gloss: Aśma: XII, 58, 2116 (Rājadh.): praises Bhīshma on his arrow-couch.
Aśmaka^1, a rājarshi, son of Vaśishṭha and Madayantī, the wife of Kalmāshapāda: I, 122, 4737 (Madayantī); 177, 6791 (Vāsishṭha) (founded Paudanya).
Aśmaka^2, a brahman present at the deathbed of Bhīshma: XII, 47, 1592 (Rājadh.) (ºSumantunā).
Aśmaka^3 (No. 46), a king of the Aśmakāḥ: VII, 37, 1606 (Abhimanyuvadhap.) (ºsya suto = No. 48 and No. 49, killed by Abhimanyu; this half-śloka is omitted in B.).
Aśmakadāyāda (No. 48): VII, 37, 1605 (Abhimanyuvadhap.) (= No. 46, ºsya suto; the reading of B. differs somewhat from that of C.).

Aśmakāḥ (No. 47), a people: VII, 85, 3049 (Jayadrathavadhap.) (in the army of the Pāṇḍavas); VIII, 8, 237 (Karṇap.) (conquered and made tributary by Karṇa); cf. No. 49 (the passages seem to contradict one another; cf. Aśvakāḥ and VP. II, 164; perhaps dwelling near Avanti or Oojein, LIA. I, 708/857).
Aśmakī, a Yādavī, the wife of king Prācinvat and mother of Saṃyāti: I, 95 (§ 156), 3766 (Pūruvaṃś.).
Aśman, a brahman consulted by Janaka Vaideha: XII, 28, 834 (Rājadh.) (ºgītam itihāsaṃ purātanam), 835 (brāhmaṇam), (837), 891.

Aśmapṛshṭha, a holy stone in Gayā (Nīl. “Pretaśilā,” the stone of the dead), a visit to which expiates the murder of a brahman: XIII, 25, 1728 (Aṅgirasas tīrthayātrāyām, v. Ānuśāsanik.). “Pret Silā exists at the present day. It is not a stone, but a rocky hill some 300 or 400 feet high.” (Grierson.)
